is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to inspect the rollout keyframes before touching the target policy. After that I’ll trace the assigned parent, sampled results, and inherited logs, implement exactly one candidate, and update both required notes files.

The contract confirms this is a single editable Julia candidate and that visual inspection must precede policy edits. I’m now anchoring the keyframes to the sampled scores, trajectory/force metrics, inherited guidance, and optimizer provenance; I’ll treat the shared prewarm sheet as common initial-condition evidence and compare the successful sample against the most informative failure.

The visual evidence is unusually consistent: every supplied released sheet is a successful diagonal, self-propelled capture, and no sampled keyframe failure exists. The strongest current rollout (`38.049` release time) and the weakest inherited success (`39.605`) follow the same topology; the weaker one shows the fish staying slightly farther from the target-directed diagonal and carries higher crossflow/load metrics. I’m using that as a regression boundary—not mislabeling it as a failure—and will now isolate which one-parameter mechanism produced the ordering.

The new evidence closes the phase-lag axis: `0.765` and `0.7675` both preserve capture but regress from exact `0.75` repeats, so the inherited quadratic-interpolation hypothesis does not survive. I’m recording that negative boundary before editing, then testing one separate, bounded tail-response axis: a small damping increase intended to reduce posterior rate/excursion while preserving the proven bearing law and route.

The candidate is now a single-axis change (`tail_damping 0.65 → 0.70`), with all other successful parameters and observations frozen. The durable guidance now closes two stale extrapolation paths—allocation below `0.35` and phase-lag interpolation above `0.75`—using the newly inherited CFD results. I’m validating the public parameter schema and running the mandated workspace checker next; no CFD will be launched.

The guidance checker passes. The policy contract command itself is currently blocked before loading the candidate because this environment has no `julia` on `PATH` (the login shell also emitted unrelated missing SSH-home setup warnings). I’m checking the workspace’s configured Julia locations and will rerun non-login if a binary is available, then continue with the boundary check.
